title: Nearby-cycle specialization preserves external products
statement:
Use the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$ and specialization of [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $\widetilde X,\widetilde Y$ be lifts over $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$, and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Then the canonical nearby-cycle external-product comparison is an isomorphism:
$$\Pi_{M,N}:\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X}M\boxtimes_A^L\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde Y}N\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X\times_D\widetilde Y}(M\boxtimes_A^LN).$$
Here the external product on the left is over $k$ between the special fibres. The map is obtained by the ordinary nearby-cycle comparisons for the two projections followed by the lax tensor map of $i^*Rj_*$, after strict henselization of $D$; thus when $X=Y$ and $\widetilde X=\widetilde Y$ with the same lift datum, it is exactly the map $\Pi$ defined in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. No properness or smoothness of either lift is assumed. This asserts external-product compatibility, not preservation of tensor products of two complexes on the same degeneration.

source.place: Proposition 3.1; geometric restriction described immediately before it; Construction 3.2 specifies comparisons. Primary publisher HTML read; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Choose bounded constructible etale representatives of $M,N$ by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. They have finite Tor amplitude by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], and admit bounded flat models $F_1,F_2$ by the etale clause of [lem-sf-flat-model]. Set $T_1=\widetilde X$, $T_2=\widetilde Y$, $B=D$, $f_i:T_i\to D$. The lift data in [def-trf-deformation-specialization] include global maps $\rho_X:T_1\to X\times_kD$ and $\rho_Y:T_2\to Y\times_kD$. Let $r_1:T_1\to X$, $r_2:T_2\to Y$ be their composites with projection. Put $L_1=r_1^*M$, $L_2=r_2^*N$. Constant-module inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so these are bounded complexes, represented by $r_i^*F_i$. On the generic fibre $r_1^*M=\rho_{X,\eta}^*M_\eta$ and $r_2^*N=\rho_{Y,\eta}^*N_\eta$, by the defining composites of the maps. Thus the geometric nearby cycles of these total-scheme inputs are precisely the two specializations of the item. The geometric generic restrictions are constructible: pull back the finite locally closed constructible partitions and their finite locally constant trivializations from [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Exact inverse image identifies their cohomology with these pullbacks.

source.place: Proposition 3.1, reduction to total-scheme inputs; here the global lift maps supply those inputs directly, and bounded flat models control the product

proof.text: The ring $k[t]_{(t)}$ is a discrete valuation ring: a nonzero polynomial is $t^r$ times a polynomial nonzero at $0$, and the latter is a unit in the localization; hence every nonzero ideal is generated by a power of $t$. The coefficient ring $A$ is finite and killed by some power of $\ell$, which is invertible on $D$ since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Apply [lem-trf-trait-nearby-base-change] to $f_1,L_1$ and $f_2,L_2$. Both pairs are $\Psi$-good. This is the substantive base-change input; it does not require the two lifts to be flat or smooth.

source.place: Example 4.26(2), verifying the Psi-goodness hypothesis cited in Lu--Zheng Proposition 3.1

proof.text:
Put $T=T_1\times_DT_2$ with structure map $f$ and projections $q_i$. For the induced maps $v_i:V_f\to V_{f_i}$, [lem-trf-good-oriented-nearby-kunneth] now gives an isomorphism
$$c:v_1^*R\Psi_{f_1}L_1\otimes_A^Lv_2^*R\Psi_{f_2}L_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Psi_f(q_1^*L_1\otimes_A^Lq_2^*L_2).$$
All its hypotheses have been checked: each $f_i$ is finite type by the lift definition, each $L_i$ is bounded by step 1, $A$ has invertible annihilator by step 2, and both pairs are $\Psi$-good. The comparison $c$ is the ordinary comparisons for $q_i$ followed by the lax tensor map, as specified in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. To justify the slice in step 4, use [lem-pc-kflat-closure]: the bounded flat models $F_i$ are K-flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], pullback along $r_iq_i$ preserves K-flatness and flat terms. Hence $q_1^*L_1\otimes_A^Lq_2^*L_2$ is represented by the total tensor of two bounded flat complexes. If their term intervals are $[a,b]$, $[c,d]$, this total complex is zero outside $[a+c,b+d]$. Thus all three inputs to the slice lemma are bounded, including the product input.

source.place: Theorem A.3(1), specialized to Y_1=Y_2=D after verifying the two independent goodness hypotheses

proof.text:
Choose the specialization $\bar\eta\to\bar0$ used in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. Pull $c$ back by $e_f:T_0\to V_f$ of [lem-trf-nearby-geometric-slice]. Functors preserve isomorphisms, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies the inverse image of the tensor with the tensor of inverse images. Since the composites $v_ie_f$ and $e_{f_i}q_{i,0}$ are induced by the same special-fibre projection and the same specialization, the uniqueness clause of the universal property [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] of the oriented product defining $V_{f_i}$ in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] identifies them. Apply the slice isomorphisms to all three nearby-cycle objects. The resulting isomorphism has source
$$q_{1,0}^*\operatorname{sp}_{T_1}M\otimes_A^Lq_{2,0}^*\operatorname{sp}_{T_2}N$$
and target $i_T^*Rj_{T*}((q_1^*L_1\otimes_A^Lq_2^*L_2)|_{T_{\bar\eta}})$. Here $T_0=X_0\times_kY_0$, with $X_0,Y_0$ denoting the special fibres of the lifts, and $i_T,j_T$ have the domains specified by the slice lemma. The pulled-back bounded flat models of step 3 give finite Tor amplitude to the generic inputs. The finiteness clause of [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange] therefore puts the two geometric specializations in $D^b_{ctf}$, so the left external product of [def-trf-external-product] is defined in its stated category.

source.place: (1.3.4), applied to the chosen geometric generic point; Lu--Zheng Section 3, restriction preceding Proposition 3.1; finite-Tor constructibility: Varshavsky 1.3.1(e), also Lu--Zheng Corollary 3.9

proof.text: The product lift has generic identification $T_\eta\simeq(X\times_kY)_\eta$. On this generic fibre, $q_i$ becomes the corresponding projection. Restricting $L_1,L_2$ gives $\rho_{X,\eta}^*M_\eta,\rho_{Y,\eta}^*N_\eta$ by step 1, and derived inverse image preserves tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Therefore the target in step 4 is $\operatorname{sp}_{T}(M\boxtimes_A^LN)$, with external product as in [def-trf-external-product]. This also checks the map, not only its endpoints. In [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], $c$ is the tensor of the two ordinary comparisons followed by the lax tensor comparison. The two compatibility clauses of [lem-trf-nearby-geometric-slice] identify these three arrows with the corresponding arrows for $i^*Rj_*$. Their composite is precisely the specified nearby-cycle external comparison in the statement. When $X=Y$ with the same lift datum, the formula for $\Pi$ in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] is that same ordered composite $t\circ(\alpha_{p_1}\otimes\alpha_{p_2})$. Thus its isomorphism is proved for the actual map $\Pi$, without claiming that either individual ordinary comparison or the lax tensor map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 3.1 and Construction 3.2, identifying the canonical comparison after geometric restriction

proof.text: Return to the pro-etale convention, when that is used. By [def-trf-deformation-specialization], each specialized object and its ordinary nearby-cycle comparisons are obtained by applying the etale/pro-etale inverse image to the etale construction just proved. Its constant-coefficient tensor comparison is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the comparison morphism of ringed topoi. It consequently identifies the etale external products and their ordered comparison composite with the pro-etale external products and their comparison. Applying this functor to the isomorphism of step 5 proves the asserted formula in the convention of the item as well. No property of tensoring two arbitrary complexes on a single degeneration has been used. The pro-etale output factors are bounded constructible by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and have finite Tor amplitude by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], applied to the etale output factors of step 4.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement and the specified comparison unchanged. Split the unconditional geometric formula into bounded generic extensions, trait Psi-goodness, the conditional oriented Kunneth theorem, and geometric slicing, including the ordinary and lax tensor maps and the finite-coefficient pro-etale interpretation. Added four statement-only/definition nodes with five actual logged searches each; no attachment or Mathlib match. Second reading uses the existing global lift maps and bounded flat models to ensure the product input is bounded before applying the slice lemma; removes the generic extension-by-zero detour. Current independent reading supplies the existing nearby-cycle finiteness citation needed by the left external-product domain, and specifies that identification with the single-functor Pi uses identical lift data.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the normal-cone specialization argument for clauses (1) and (2) in the current lem-trf-local-term-locality proof: external-product compatibility required by lem-trf-trace-specialization. This is below the unit route and uses no smooth-purity replacement.

tool_uses.why: Generic finite-coefficient etale-origin equivalence selects the representatives prescribed by the specialization definition; this unit contains no such equivalence.
Generic derived monoidality of pullback on ringed topoi identifies tensors after geometric slicing and after the etale/pro-etale comparison; the unit has no statement at this generality.
Exact inverse image in constant module coefficients applies to the global lift maps, with no flatness assumption on the scheme morphism.
Transfers the given finite Tor amplitude to the etale representatives before selecting bounded flat models.
The etale bounded flat model theorem ensures the total tensor is bounded, as required by the geometric slice statement.
Bounded flat complexes are K-flat, so their ordinary total tensor computes derived tensor.
